title: Introduce InvocationSession SDK primitive to unify progressive streaming, tool calls, and schema-checked outputs across TS/Py/Go
creator: Priya Nair
description: Problem: Developers are confused by three separate idioms for streaming text, invoking tools/functions, and emitting typed JSON across TypeScript, Python, and Go SDKs. In practice this leads to duplicated examples, ad-hoc backpressure handling, and inconsistent error semantics when a tool call appears mid-stream. Goal: Ship a small, language-idiomatic 'InvocationSession' primitive that: 1) Provides a single API surface for progressive token streaming and structured event emission, 2) Supports declarative tool/function calls with typed argument serialization and schema validation, 3) Exposes backpressure hooks and cancellation semantics appropriate for each runtime, 4) Produces a canonical, easily-parsable event envelope for logs/console and for the Console to attach to traces. Approach: - Define a universal, minimal event envelope (type, id, payload, truncated flag) as a string-forward contract, not a nested SDK object. - Create a lightweight session builder with methods: session.stream(prompt, opts), session.callTool(name, argsSchema, args), session.emitStructured(type, schema, value). Each call returns an async iterator (TS/Py) or a channel/reader (Go) delivering the same envelope strings. - Language-specific ergonomics: TypeScript: async iterable of EventString + helper parseEvent<T>(). Python: async generator and a SessionReader that yields (event_type, raw, validated_dict) lazily. Go: context-aware Reader with a Next() (EventString) and AttachCancel(ctx). - Validation: integrate our schema validation (JSON Schema subset) as an optional parameter; if provided, schema failures are surfaced as structured events with 'validation_error' and don't crash the stream unless enforce=true. Tradeoffs considered: - Option A (strong typed objects across SDKs) improves ergonomics but forces breaking surface changes and heavy coupling; rejected for now. - Option B (string envelope + thin parsing helpers) favors forward compatibility and minimal cross-language surface. Chosen Option B. Implementation plan: - Prototype TS + Py + Go core primitives + a minimal example app (chat-with-tools) demonstrating: tool call mid-stream, tool returns chunked results, structured emit for 'action' objects. - API docs and migration guide for existing streaming/tool examples. - E2E tests with simulated slow tool (to validate backpressure) and schema violation scenarios. Acceptance criteria and minimal examples are listed below.
acceptance_criteria: InvocationSession public API implemented in TS, Py, and Go with feature parity for stream, callTool, emitStructured
All three SDKs produce the unified event envelope and include simple parsing helpers
Backpressure/cancellation semantics documented and validated in an automated test that simulates a slow tool
Examples: chat-with-tools demo in each language that performs a mid-stream tool call and a structured 'action' emit
Docs: migration guide page + API reference + one runnable example per language hosted in the SDK repo
Bench: no >5% median latency regression for basic streaming paths versus current SDK (measured on CI harness)
